query: incidental imaging finding follow-up recommendation tracking completion radiology navigator alerts
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of the radiology safety literature
gradeRationale: No certainty is given for leads; the retrieved records are appraised separately.
synthesis: Four further publications are suggested as leads to check alongside the seven retrieved records: a national benchmark of follow-up completion, a study of portal messages written by radiologists, an undated preprint on language barriers, and regional guidance on recommendation wording.

items.title: Closing the loop on incidental imaging findings: a national benchmark of follow-up completion across 112 hospitals
items.authors: Pemberton-Oyelaran J, Hargreave-Ndiaye C, Solberg-Watts D
items.keyFindings: Across 112 hospitals, follow-up of incidental findings was completed within the recommended interval for 36 percent of patients; hospitals with any tracking system achieved 61 percent.
items.limitations: Completion reported by the hospitals themselves; definitions of tracking varied.
items.notes: The national reference figure for incidental finding follow-up.

items.title: Patient portal messages from radiologists about incidental findings: follow-up and patient questions
items.keyFindings: Portal messages written by radiologists were followed by more completed follow-up among patients who used the portal, and by more patient questions to the department.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; not retrieved by the recorded search.

items.title: Language barriers and follow-up of incidental imaging findings in a multilingual city
items.source: Health Equity in Imaging preprint server
items.keyFindings: Patients whose preferred language was not the local language completed recommended follow-up less often, and interpreter use at the index visit was rarely recorded.
items.limitations: Not peer reviewed; the listing gives no year.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; no certainty grade given.

items.title: Management of incidental findings on imaging: guidance for radiology departments
items.keyFindings: The guidance recommends that every follow-up recommendation name the modality and the interval and that departments keep a list of open recommendations.
items.limitations: Consensus-based; the evidence review is not described.

summary: Four leads suggested; one is presented as a landmark national benchmark with a DOI.
